fb: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs

Ephron the Hittite sold Abraham the cave of Machpelah at Hebron, and Uriah, the soldier whose wife David took, was a Hittite too. Critics once doubted there was ever a Hittite nation, until digs at Boghazkoy in Turkey found its capital. The Hittites in Canaan were probably a smaller offshoot, or the name used loosely.

H2809.d: Cheshbon, a place East of the Jordan
fb: Sihon's capital, east of the Jordan near the northern edge of Moab. Moses took it before Israel crossed into Canaan, and it became a Levitical city in Reuben. Moab later had it back, which is why the prophets name it in their judgments on Moab, and the ruins, still called Hesban, lie about twenty miles east of the Jordan.

H2832.d: Chasmonah, a place in the Desert
fb: One of the stops on the wilderness route, a little before Moseroth and near Mount Hor. The name may have to do with fatness or fruitfulness, and nobody knows where it was.

H2826.d: to make (intrans. be) unsteady, i.e. weak

fb: One of the southernmost towns given to Judah in the Negev, toward the border of Edom, and nobody has found where it was.

Sisera's base, the Canaanite general who led Jabin's iron chariots. Barak broke his army at the Kishon and chased what was left back here. Where exactly it was is still argued over, near Mount Carmel or a district name for several settlements.

H2888.d: Tabbath, a place East of the Jordan
fb: When Gideon's three hundred broke the Midianite camp, the army ran toward Tabbath, near the Jordan south of Beth-shean.

H2872.d: properly, accumulated; i.e. (by implication) a summit

H2897.d: Tob, a region apparently East of the Jordan
fb: Jephthah's half-brothers drove him out for being a prostitute's son, and he went to the land of Tob, east of Gilead. He gathered outlaws there until Gilead's elders came to fetch him back to fight the Ammonites. Men of Tob later hired themselves out to the Ammonites.
A forest in Judah. David hid there with his growing band after leaving his parents with the king of Moab, and the prophet Gad told him to go. Where it was is unknown.

H2843.d: a Chushathite or descendant of Chushah
fb: Two of David's mighty men carry this label, Sibbecai and Mebunnai, and it ties them to Hushah in Judah's genealogy. Sibbecai is also the one who killed a Philistine giant in a later battle at Gob.
